text_fidelity_a:
LUBAN 35 LB Adjustable Dumbbell and Kettlebell for Men and Women, Perfect for Home, Office, Gym Work Out I already had a Bowflex adjustable kettlebell that I liked a lot (though it's not perfect), but I wanted another adjustable kettlebell with lower weights for certain types of work. After four months of regular use, it's still in good shape and I'm glad I bought it.

Changing the plates is not as fast as on the Bowflex model, but it's easy, although the sliding tab sticks now and then. Still, it's fast enough for me to continue through a circuit without losing momentum, and that's what's important to me.

All the plates weight 2.5 lbs, and you can remove them however you like. That is, you don't have to take them from the top or the bottom. You will have to slot them back into the same place they came from, however, because they all curve in a certain way to give the kettlebell it's shape. The reviewer who mentioned sharp edges makes a good point, one worth considering for different exercises. For example, for swings it makes no difference to me where I pull the plates from, but if I'm doing shoulder presses, I pull them from the bottom or else I'll get my forearm unpleasantly poked and scraped as I use it. For a bottoms up carry, I find keeping the plates loaded at the top makes the weight more stable as I walk.

The plates make a slight rattle when swung -- that doesn't bother me, but it's something to keep in mind if working out within earshot of someone who might be disturbed by the noise. The plates do feel secure within the bell, but I still make it a habit to swing it so that the plates would fly away from me rather than at me if they came loose, and I swing them toward a wall or some other area where the plate wouldn't damage anyone. All that said, I'm sure I'm being overly cautious.

One thing I really like about this is the overall shape and footprint as compared to the Bowflex adjustable kettlebell. This one is a standard kettlebell size -- that makes it easier for me to handle, especially when it's in close to my body. The Bowflex is much larger, and that makes certain moves really awkward. It's not fair to compare these, though, given that they have very different weight ranges, but it's something I noticed. In those few places where the weights overlap, I almost always reach for this kettlebell over the Bowflex.

When buying exercise equipment, I'd much rather go to a shop where I can try it out in person and comparison shop. The pandemic made that impossible, so I crossed my fingers and hoped for the best. And it worked out. Even with its flaws, I've definitely gotten my money's worth for this.
text_fidelity_b: LUBAN 35 LB Adjustable Dumbbell and Kettlebell for Men and Women, Perfect for Home, Office, Gym Work Out

LIGHTBAR | LED Headlamp, 300 to 500 Lumens, Spot Light Mode and Red Light Modes Available On Select Models - Perfect for Camping Running Biking Fishing Construction I've had this for a couple of months, but just used it for the first time this past weekend while camping with friends. I will never use it for that again.

A) The wide angle sounds like a good thing, but it was really annoying to my friends. I had to keep the headlamp at the lowest possible brightness, and even then the light shining so wide was still annoying to everyone around me.

B) The led strip is very thin, resulting in the light source being behind the plane of my glasses. So much light was reflecting off the lenses of my glasses back into my eyes that I truly couldn't see much of anything in front of me. There's no point lighting a path if I still can't actually see the path.

Also, this headlamp has a proprietary charger. So you have to keep that specific single-use cable with you in order to recharge the batteries. And the batteries drain even when not in use. I charged it fully when I first got it a couple of months ago. Fortunately I tested it before my camping trip and discovered it was completely drained. So you can't just charge it and expect it to be ready when you need it. I had to fully charge it just before I left.

It is really very bright, so if you need something really bright, and you don't have glasses, and there's no one else around you who might be blinded by your headlight, then it might be an ok choice for you. But with so very many options out there, I recommend you keep looking. There are definitely better choices than this.
text_fidelity_b: LIGHTBAR | LED Headlamp, 300 to 500 Lumens, Spot Light Mode and Red Light Modes Available On Select Models - Perfect for Camping Running Biking Fishing Construction

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Flex 2, Navy (US Version) This is my second Fitbit but my first Fitbit Flex (I have used the One in the past). I really like it and haven't had any problems with the accuracy.

I love the community involved when you use the Fitbit brand (challenges with friends and family to keep you going). I REALLY like that this is water proof- I haven't gone swimming with it on yet, but it's nice that I don't have to think about it when I shower or when I'm washing the dishes.

It is a relatively small and simple design. There are 5 lights on the top, 4 to indicate the proportion of your daily steps you've done that day (with the goal of 10,000) and the fifth to give you notices. You have to remember what each of the colors is, but I haven't had any problems with that- green to indicate when you're checking on your steps, red to tell you your battery is getting low, and blue or purple when you're getting a phone call or text (I'm not totally sure about these as I don't use them for that). You can connect to you phone to notify you when you get a phone call or text message; you get get hourly reminders to move; you can track your sleep schedule; and what I love the most about is that you can seamlessly change activity type (running, elliptical, swimming, outdoor biking) without manipulating the information on your app.

Easy and comfortable. I have definitely found that it has helped me increase my daily steps!
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Flex 2, Navy (US Version)

Relentless Tactical The Defender Leather IWB Holster - Fits Most 1911 Style Handguns - Kimber - Colt - S & W - Sig Sauer - Remington - Ruger & More - Made in USA Relentless Tactical is well-known for it's reasonably priced yet high quality holsters. This particular model is designed to fit "most 1911 style handguns". What I found out is a bit different. This holster is very particular with which pistols it provides the right fit for. Although some of the larger guns can be slipped inside it, there is not a tight enough fit to hold these guns when the holster is held upside down.

What I did find that seems to fit well include the following: Kahr CM9, Glock 42, Colt Defender, and surprisingly my old Cobray double barrel .410/45LC derringer. Of course trying to withdraw and safely shoot this derringer in a tactical situation could lead to some potentially horrible mistakes. If indeed you manage to get that gun safely on target, the person on the receiving end would probably faint just from the fireball.

Although I tried several others in my collection (Glock 19, Colt Commander, Walther P22, Springfield XDS, H&K VP9SK, etc.) none of them properly/safely fit this holster. The next step up would be important and I'm sure that Relentless would be happy to point you in the correct direction. They also offer a 100% satisfaction guarantee with no questions asked. Good people to deal with!
text_fidelity_b: Relentless Tactical The Defender Leather IWB Holster - Fits Most 1911 Style Handguns - Kimber - Colt - S & W - Sig Sauer - Remington - Ruger & More - Made in USA

Sivan Health and Fitness Balance Ball Fit Chair Base with Ball & Pump I love that it doesn't have a back and it is so reasonably priced! At first the ball seems small, but after a couple of days if you add more air the ball will become large in size. In fact, I had to deflate it some as it became too tall to sit on and I was leaning over my desk. It is common, at least with the balance balls that I have owned, to have a break in period.
You have to allow the material to stretch and soften. This material is made to be flexible and stretch with your body weight. As for the locks on the wheels, they are annoying, but I do understand their purpose. I used some twisty ties to tie them up until I wish to use them. So far they have not come down.
All in all this is a great chair, especially if you like to wiggle on a balance ball instead of being stationary. I find myself moving around from side to side and bouncing every so slightly the whole time I am sitting on it, except while I am typing.
If you are they fidgeting type of person, this chair will make you very happy.
I did buy the cover by Gaiam that is velvety and it is a little large for this ball, but I was able to make adjustments to the cover and it looks great on the chair.

text_fidelity_a:
Coleman Camping Instant Signal Mountain Tent Prior to getting this tent we borrowed a tent for a camping trip, and while we thought it set up quick and seemed nice, we were greeted by a deluge pouring through the seams on the roof. My wife was about ready to swear off camping, but we pushed on. We weren't going to let that happen again, so when I saw this tent, I pounced.

It comes in a rather large box, and the bag within is big for a four person tent, but not too large. The real bonus was the expanding bottom of the bag, which makes it nice and neat for before the sale but expands to be a more realistic container after the first trip, where things don't tend to fit in their original bags.

That trip was eye opening. Not only is the sixty second assembly more or less legit (it kinda doubles when you include taking it out of the bag), it's an ample tent. I'm 6'7" and while I couldn't stand in in the tent, it's broad tall roof is such a blessing. Likewise the sides go up at a steep angle making all but the outer inches rather tall too. It's nice and airy and makes a very generous two person tent, though you could turn it into a flop house and squeeze 4 in. I'd say 4 is doable, and 2 is luxurious, which is more than I'd say for any 4 person tents. Well done!

No leaks, quick setup, quick break down, and stylish looks are a big pluses.

Minuses are few and minor--mostly size of tent for storage (as the description notes, this isn't for backpacking). It's not the most compact, but really it's a slight difference and the quick setup is a great trade off and makes you want to actually use the tent!
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Camping Instant Signal Mountain Tent

I had tried another one meant for the car, also with a USB cord and while it warmed, the part against my back began to dig into my back and hurt.  I mean, it may have been a bit more padded than this one, but it had no "give" so that I didn't feel IT under me, if that makes sense. Cycled through the three heating levels - green, blue and red - the red had the back of my legs (through pants) almost burning!  So red may be perfect for those really, really cold nights.  The green which appears to be the lightest heating just barely seemed to warm my backside, but the blue level, as Goldilocks would say was just right.  I felt the heat, but it wasn't so hot that it bothered my skin.  For my purpose, this is so much better than a heating pad - they require a three-prong outlet and the one I was using had to constantly be rearranged as it would fall down as soon as I got up.  It heated well, but jeez, why do I want to futz with a heating pad every single time I get up out of my chair?  This, being made for a chair is sitting and staying put just fine!  I am happy with this heated pad for a chair - indoors or out.

The front light does a VERY good job of keeping the city streets in view. It is 3x as bright as the typical tiny lights people add to their city commuting bikes and it can be seen from blocks away. You can be sure cars headed towards you will be aware of your presence.

The rear light has a large number of flash patterns and brightness settings. Its also a decent size, so you can be sure you're visible from the rear.

The kit includes extra fastening material for the front and rear lights - which is a GREAT addition.

Battery life seems appropriate. We've used it for three evenings of 30 minute commuting and have not had to recharge yet.

Recommended.

text_fidelity_a: FlipKlip Treadmill Book Holder 1-Pak This is a product that I want to love, and wants to be useful...and comes very close- but just misses the mark.  I use it for holding open those sheet music books that a certain music book publisher (I won't name names but it kinda rhymes with Cal Centered)seems to refuse to put in spiral bound form... ARRRGH nothing worse than trying to play a guitar when the book keeps closing on you.  I've tried everything I can think of to keep the pages open.  Closepins, those metal music stand arms, metal 3 pronged page clips, paperclips, spring clips.... heck even rubberbands.  This little gadget is probably the best solution so far (but not perfect). It will hold the book open (yea) but often times with sheet music you gotta flip back and forth between pages- this is difficult (not impossible, but does mess up the flow of the music). text_fidelity_a:
NIKINER Women's Classic Roller Skates Premium High-top Leather Roller Skates for Women Men Double Row Shiny Indoor Outdoor Skates for Unisex Girls with Shoes Bag [[VIDEOID:6a9dae27c4383bb5bbbf63af76ea0b65]] A year ago my wife was using roller blades, but wanting a pair of roller skates to also enjoy. A year ago, she severely broke her foot and was sidelined for seven months, but limited as she came back. Now she’s able to do more, cleared for roller blading, but she had been wanting those skates... so when I had the chance to grab her this pair, I took it. She had to wait awhile, but now she’s had a chance to get on them... These NIKINER Women's Classic Roller Skates Premium High-top Leather Roller Skates are decent, what she described as good for beginners and moderate skaters, but she had a few things to mention. First, she has a foot size that can be spot on 9 or 9.5 with a range that could workout between, based on the show and it's cut. In this case, ordering online, she wasn’t able to try them on first. In the end, she feels like the overall fit around the foot is good, but snug. The front of the boot - at the toes - is the tightest. She first tried with thicker socks, but settled for compression socks, which worked much better. Leather can sometimes adjust to a foot, stretching a bit to hug a foot, but in this case, we’re not sure. She says the front at the toes is tough - the leather hard - so she can’t imagine it stretching. In the end, she feels like if you’re spot on a size, you should be okay, but if there is even a slight “off” about a foot size, there could be an issue.

Second, The skates look nice, and overall the materials. - leather - seems good. The materials in the base and wheels seem good. They have wheels that are supposed to light up as they role - they do, but it’s hard to see in the light/daylight. We have not tried them in the dark, and we do see a little sparkle, but overall, you’re not going to be rolling in the dark, so what we are seeing, it’s not overly impressive. There is a little video above, but yea, the “light up” to us is not impressive. Third, She loved roller skating as a child through to young adult and wants to go back to doing it again. She loves loves loves roller blading, but there is something about skating she holds dear... We will say, her being unable to do anything like this in a year has made it hard for her - she felt it hard/big/painful and has to take this slowly getting back to it. She got up, she went, and she really liked it a lot. She felt like it’s coming back and she enjoyed the experience. She feels like these NIKINER Women's Classic Roller Skates Premium High-top Leather Roller Skates are going to let her get back up and going - with time to develop - and she’s going to be able to enjoy it. But she also feels like these are beginner to moderate level. The ground itself - the surface - is important. The place we took them (parking lot) was rough and uncomfortable for her. She does have an area she loves for blading, but during several months a year (current) we have a massive amount of acorns that fall and she cannot, for safety, blade (or roller skate) in the area. So this parking lot showed her not every surface is going to work with these skates.

Overall, these ARE decent skates. Things to consider: size, type of sock, surface for skating. These will have an affect on the experience. She sets them best for beginner to moderate. And in the end, she does like them and thinks she’ll get a good amount of use out of them.
text_fidelity_b: NIKINER Women's Classic Roller Skates Premium High-top Leather Roller Skates for Women Men Double Row Shiny Indoor Outdoor Skates for Unisex Girls with Shoes Bag

Texsport Portable Outdoor Camping Shower Privacy Shelter Changing Room, Gray, 1 Count (Pack of 1) Most of the state parks here in CA have their showers turned off due to the drought, or want you to pay $2 for a 2 minute shower. This item makes for a great changing room for those that have smaller tents and can't stand up. The floor liner is VERY slippery once wet. Keep your sandals on when showering. It's also very important to place on as level a surface as possible. Due to our campsite configuration we couldn't get a perfect spot so I found myself fighting a little bit to not slip. You can easily get two normal length showers out of one bag. The bags are VERY heavy when completely filled. If you aren't that tall you may need some help hanging the bag.

Pros: Light, easy to set up, price
Cons: Once the shower bag is mounted, the end of the nozzle was already down to my chest. Get used to squatting, holding one hand on the nozzle and the other hand lathering or rinsing yourself. This can get very hard if you have long hair you are trying to shampoo.

Suggestions:
1. Make a more horizontal shower bag so that it doesn't hang so low.
2. A towel rack inside would be nice. In all honestly, there isn't enough water flow to get anything else wet. I used the mesh toiletry bags for my dry clothes.

text_fidelity_a:
Osprey Unisex-Adult Daypack Backpacks I had a hard time finding a pack to replace my Jansport Penelope 34. I needed something at least that size or bigger and that proved more difficult than expected. I had no idea my pack would be considered so large, it barely fit everything I needed as it is! I only gave it 4 stars because it has only a very small pouch for school supplies. While I understand that it isn't necessarily built for a student, it does have a pouch for a laptop so I guess I assumed it would be more business/student friendly.

In any case, it's large enough but that space is much taller than it is wide. So far, it seems to fit everything I need. I put 2 medium sized text books, 2 spiral bound single subject notebooks, a novel sized book, a 13'' mac in the laptop sleeve and a spiral bound textbook with room to spare. Empty, it's much lighter than my JanSport pack which I appreciate.

It seems to be very well made but I wish it had some of the features of their other packs like the pockets on the waist strap or shoulder straps. It'd be nice to have my phone in front of me instead of in the pack itself but I guess that's what pockets are for. There are 2 stretchy water bottle pockets that seem to accommodate large bottles but they are hard to reach and impossible to put back without taking the pack off. At least that's what I've found out carrying a 1 liter sized bottle today.

The color is gorgeous! I love, love, LOVE it! It's a very deep aqua/turquoise color that's not overly bright or obnoxious. It's seriously one of the nicest looking packs I found in this price range when shopping and I looked at everyone and I mean EVERYONE! I spent about 2 days doing research and this was one of the best deals for the most volume out there. Overall, I think most students would be happy with it but it might be considered very large if you don't pack your books around all day. I carpool so I get dropped off at school in the morning and don't leave until early evening. I need to take all my books, workout clothes, food etc... So this pack still might be a little tight for all that but we'll see.

UPDATED 08/28/14

The bag has held up extremely well. I questioned how the elastic pockets on the front and sides would hold up and they seem to be just fine. After having it for a year I have to say the shape is frustrating. It's too tall and narrow so it wastes too much space. I find myself having to stack things on top of my books to take full advantage of the size of the bag. Other than that, it's been comfortable, kept my stuff dry on rainy days and still looks new! I'm glad I'm graduating in December because I'd probably want to buy another bag and I don't think my husband would appreciate that very much ;-)
text_fidelity_b: Osprey Unisex-Adult Daypack Backpacks

There have been many times when testing the best way to use this when the steps showed zero when I checked it. In order to not over count steps due to random movement, the steps are not counted until you've done 10 similar steps in a row. Since I do a lot of work in the kitchen and gardening that is under 10 steps, then a pause, then more steps, this means a lot of steps are not being counted. Also, it seems like it is not counting those first 10 steps, either. If I step 50 steps in a row, it only counts like 32 steps. Frankly, an app on my phone works better than this. I had thought a dedicated device would work better, but I guess not. I will note that it seems to count steps better when this is clipped to my shoe rather than to my waistband. I'll update after little bit if I figure out how to make it work better.

The step counter comes with a battery, and you remove the plastic strip preventing connection in order to turn on the pedometer. It is then constantly on, though it does go into a sleep mode when there is no movement. The instructions that come with it are not very clear, but you're supposed to be able to set things like stride length. You hit the mode button to switch between steps, distance, calories burned, time spent walking, speed, the clock, and total steps. There is also a reset button along one edge and a set button along with other edge. You can remove the counter from the clip (mainly to access the battery chamber). My accidental reset problem has been when the buttons are near the top of the clip, where you have to squeeze to release the clip. I still seem to bump the buttons when the ends are switched, but it's not as often.
text_fidelity_b: New Balance Step Counter Pedometer - Belt Clipon Pedometer Fitness Tracker Walking Meter with Removable Base Ideal for Women, Men, Kids to Count Steps, Distance, Calories Burned & Time, Black/Red

JOOLA Tour Elite Pro Pickleball Bag – Backpack & Duffle Bag for Paddles & Pickleball Accessories – Thermal Insulated Pockets Hold 4+ Paddles - Includes Fence Hook I am so impressed with and excited about this JOOLA Tour Elite Pro Pickleball Bag in a dark blue with a bright yellow-green accent that I can’t wait to get back onto the court. My wife and I have recently taken up the sport and wanted bags to not just carry our stuff, but store it off the court, and carry the various things we end up having with, based on that days activities. This JOOLA Tour Elite Pro Pickleball Bag hits all the checks for us.

It has a great look. That dark blue and yellow-green are so nice together - they look good in pictures, but great in person. One wouldn’t think such a bright color would be appealing, but it is, and as my wife always points out, a lighter color for the interior of a bag makes it that much easier to see inside - including those dark corners. There are plenty of corners here. The inside of the main compartment has several pockets with zippers to keep things in place, offering places for things like wallet, keys, and other little items you end up carrying. Bring the extra set of clothes? There is plenty of room to keep things in place. This main compartment is huge and we can easily get in another set of clothes and even toiletry bag in there to make changing easy. There is one of those shoe slots - the in thing for all gym bags - which always take up space in the main bag, but keeps your shoes separate from your clothes - and there reminds plenty of room in the bag even when full. The shoe bag - accessed from the exterior - has a little venting hole for keeping smells in check. The zippers throughout the JOOLA Tour Elite Pro Pickleball Bag are good - they are solid and well constructed like the rest of the bag, meaning we should get a good, long life out of it, whatever we throw at it. In fact, all the materials, construction, and design are outstanding. The outside of the bag is symmetrical, with matching slots/pockets on each side for your rackets and other items. Based on the depth and width, we’d carry balls in the main compartment, but the outside offers plenty of options. For the racket you’ll get sharped pockets with that kind of material you find inside a lot of cooler/cooler bags - the silver material that keeps it cool, allegedly for keeping your racket in a “temperate controlled” slot. Didn’t even think about having rackets stay ‘cool,’ but there you go. The JOOLA Tour Elite Pro Pickleball Bag also offers a major, hard plastic hook in its own zippered pocket on the backside. You’ll be able to hang the bag, or set it, whatever you need, but do so with confidence of the quality of materials here. The bag also comes with not merely the handle on the top, but backpack straps to let you carry it with ease. Again, like the rest of the materials, the backpack straps are well made and should be comfortable for hauling around on your back.

In the end, this JOOLA Tour Elite Pro Pickleball Bag is excellent and I’m thrilled to have it. We may be new to the sport of pickleball, but we’ve both spent our lives as athletes of various sports and had many bags over the years. I'm used to the ways of a good bag and thrilled with how well done this JOOLA Tour Elite Pro Pickleball Bag is, how great it looks, and how it’ll make carrying my gear easy.
text_fidelity_b: JOOLA Tour Elite Pro Pickleball Bag – Backpack & Duffle Bag for Paddles & Pickleball Accessories – Thermal Insulated Pockets Hold 4+ Paddles - Includes Fence Hook

text_fidelity_a:
MaxxHaul 50027 Hitch Mount Bike Rack Platform Style 2-Bike Rack for Cars Trucks SUVs Minivans with Hitch Tightener I have this rack mounted on the front of my truck and recently used it for the first time on a 1200 mile round trip. It is built so that it is not too bulky, yet is sturdy enough for it's purpose. Assembly was straight forward and took about 20 minutes from the time I opened the box. It does have more play in it than I liked out of the box but with slight adjustments I had no issues with it shaking or rattling.
1) I used the included ubolt and bracket to eliminate any up and down movement at the receiver. This is a bit of a pain to take on and off if you want to remove the whole rack when you get to your destination but it works well.
2) It had a bit of front to back movement at the pivot/hinge bolt that is used to tilt the rack. Since I don't need it to tilt at all, I tightened this bolt so that it no longer has any movement at this point.
3) Since it uses pins to assemble the pole and wheel supports there was still some side to side movement to the whole rack. I looped a tie down strap back to my tow hooks on each side so that it couldn't move back and forth.

It would be nice if it was a tight fit everywhere but it was REALLY nice to now pay several hundred dollars. For the cost of this rack I am very happy with the value I received.

text_fidelity_a:
Timex Full-Size Ironman Road Trainer Heart Rate Monitor A good heart rate monitor and watch for people into fitness but are not super serious athletes. You can also wear this watch as a nice, functional regular watch too.

The operation of this watch is similar to the basic Timex ironman watches with some additional features (it's necessary to read the manual to understand all the features).

Pros: Watch is very comfortable - it's big but it stays in place. The strap is very adjustable and should fit nearly every wrist. The heart rate strap is also comfortable. The large face is a bonus because it's that much easier to glance down and see the numbers when you're running.
Lots of features - Chrono counts time and records your total workout length or laps, and gives an average HR for each lap. The interval timer counts down and can do timed intervals (eg. run for 8 min, walk 30 seconds). The review feature will give you average HR, max/min HR for the workout, how many minutes you spent in your "target" HR and calories burnt, which is nice to see if you want to judge how intense your workout was. It also gives the average HR for each of your laps.

It has an alarm clock and a really good Indiglo setting for the dark.

Very easy to use the HR monitor, basically put it on and press the HR button on the watch and it automatically starts getting HR data.

Cons: The review feature doesn't give the time spent in each HR zone over the whole workout, only your target HR zone. This seems like a big oversight because it's as important to see how much time you spend in the high HR "red" zones as well as the lower zones. This means that if you're running up and down varied terrain, you have to look down at your wrist to see what your HR is and remember what zone that is for you and guess how much time you've spent in each zone.

If you're only using one of the interval timers, you have to set the second interval timer to 0, which is very annoying. It would be easy to have a feature asking if you want to use one or two timers.

It doesn't store more than 1 workout review in the watch, so you have to write the info down if you want a record of your workouts. This is ridiculous for a watch at this price point.

It's not ANT+ compatible, so there's no way to increase the functionality like tying it to a GPS device. I suppose they want you to buy the next level up if you want to record that type of fitness data.
text_fidelity_b: Timex Full-Size Ironman Road Trainer Heart Rate Monitor

text_fidelity_a:
Dietz #30 Little Wizard Oil Lamp Burning Lantern Blue (Small Tank) Fantastic lantern. If you're used to standard big-box-retailer fare, this lantern is a HUGE step up in quality and size and you'll be very pleasantly surprised. I've burned it ~12 hours and have yet to notice a drop in the fuel level. No smell when burning(except for a few hours after the very first use), even on plain ole kerosene. While it's attractively built and painted, this lantern is clearly built to be used, not just displayed. Packaging was GREAT, I was really surprised at how well this lantern was packaged.

Tips for use: The wick will probably need to be trimmed when you receive it, mine was uneven and had many loose threads. I used angle nippers, a sharp pair of scissors will do better. I just removed the whole burner assembly for easier access and trimmed the wick level with the wick tube. Burn it for several hours the first time OUTSIDE. The paint will be doing it's final outgassing upon being heated and greases and oils from stamping will be burning off during this period, you don't want that going on in your house. When you first light this lantern, turn it up a little bit and let the whole lantern heat up for 10-15 minutes before turning the lantern up to full brightness. Likewise when putting out the lantern, turn it down to a very low flame and let the lantern cool for a few minutes before actually blowing it out. The flame doesn't actually burn liquid fuel, it burns fuel that's vaporized off the wick. If you just blow out the lantern, full throttle to blown out, a bunch of that fuel is still vaporizing off the wick and that smells bad. This can be mitigated considerably by turning down the lantern and letting it cool, which will reduce the amount of fuel that continues to be vaporized after the flame is finally blown out. Odor may be less of an issue with lamp oil, but even with lamp oil, you'll still be inhaling the vaporized lamp oil, even if you're not smelling it. Not healthy.

Now, the one reason I gave 4 stars instead of 5 was that there was a chip down to bare metal on the font when the lantern arrived. As stated above, the packaging was amazing and undamaged, this lantern clearly sustained this chip before being shipped. I used a dab of nailpolish that was fairly close to the color to prevent rust in the future. This did not effect the use of the lantern at all, and I will be buying more.

5/21/16 update: I have several gallons of kerosene through this lantern now. Lantern has performed flawlessly, but I have found that it is actually my least used lantern. It's about the same size, weight, and cost as an Air Pilot, but puts out ~1/2 the light. Yes it burns less fuel, but if you turn down an Air Pilot to the same light level, you'll get about the same fuel consumption while still having the option to turn it up and get more light if you need/want.
text_fidelity_b: Dietz #30 Little Wizard Oil Lamp Burning Lantern Blue (Small Tank)

Battery lanterns are great and all, but there are times you can't go get more and you end up with nothing. I love solar, so I figured this would be a great way to go. text_fidelity_a:
Intex Mariner Inflatable Boat Set Series I live in an apartment in Arizona, and I wanted a quality inflatable boat I could take to the local lakes. After researching my options, IM4 appeared to be the top boat.

Although manufacturer claims it is a 4 person boat, it is NOT true. Two people can be comfortable in this boat, three is pushing it. With the semi-solid floor the boat is stable on the lakes; however, you cannot stand or dance as some reviewers claim. Solid floor allows it some degree of stability, but not enough to stand up or walk while being fully upright.

The hull materials and ores supplied are very good. Boat has a solid feel to it. When inflating it to the max, it become very firm- raft like.

For $220 this is an amazing deal. I would recommend this boat!

Update from 10/05/2012. On my recent trip to the lake I broke one of the ores. The plastic on the coupling broke when I did five spirited rows, I was upset. I had to try to canoe paddle the boat to shore and mend the plastic coupling with some duct tape! Upon returning home I checked the Intex's website for the replacement coupling; it is being sold for $4+ shipping. Can't blame the boat for the broken ore, plastic coupling is the cheapest part of this boat.
text_fidelity_b: Intex Mariner Inflatable Boat Set Series

text_fidelity_a:
Champion Eclipse Graphite Complete Pickleball Set | Includes 3.0 Portable Net System + 4 Graphite Pickleball Paddles + 4 Outdoor Pickleballs + Pickleball Duffel Bag + USAPA Rulebook After weeks of bad weather and then surgery (and recovery) and then more bad weather, we finally had a day we could get out with this Champion Eclipse Graphite Complete Pickleball Set and give it a try. We did end up trying the paddles separate from the net (long story), but find both parts of this set really good and when we do get the chance to actual use the paddles with the net, it’ll be great. For what my wife and I consider a “beginner” and/or at home set, this is a really nice offering.

First, the “tools.” This set includes a bag (for these items), Rulebook, 4 paddles, 4 balls. All beginner level, if you get into pickle ball you’ll likely find yourself looking to upgrade, but for the backyard, for beginners, for kids or adults getting into this fast growing sport, this Champion Eclipse Graphite Complete Pickleball Set will get you off on the right foot. My wife and I are technically beginners, but we have played (not a lot), but we already do prefer longer paddles - yet we found these were good for practice. The weight is not bad, and overall they worked great. For adults or kids, they should work fine. The balls work. We play outdoors and they were fine for us. We actually got this set (primarily) for the net. The community where we live has 2 tennis courts, but also a lot of people who play tennis (most communities we’ve lived in no one does). So we wanted to have something we could take to a local park or parking lot and be able to play (we will return to club play when this Covid stuff... gets better). But we’ve used these balls and paddle on the tennis courts and they worked fine. The bag for the paddle and balls works well. It’s not top of the line, but it works fine and we’ll keep these in it for a quick grab and go.

The big plus for us was the rule book. Again, we’re only starting out and played some club stuff just before Covid. This is letting us get up to speed ahead of getting back to thing. So thrilled that was included.

The Net: this was what we really got the Champion Eclipse Graphite Complete Pickleball Set for. Again, our tennis courts can fill up when the weather allows and we were not getting any time. So we thought let’s try it. We come away very impressed. The bag it comes in is solid, well made, and while the net is slightly heavy, to us it means the materials are substantial, but not so heavy a lot of people would have an issue. We didn’t weight it, but my wife and I are guessing around 15 - 20 lbs. It did take some time to set up the first time. Working through the steps and matching the pieces - it ended up being really easy, but everything is slow going that first time. I think substantial is the best word here. We have tried a few volleyball and badminton nets and came away underwhelmed or sort of happy. This net is very good. The pieces are metal, well marked, and well designed. We set it up at the park where there was shade (our hot weather state has been off the charts hot), and got it together in less than 10 minutes - that was with undoing things for the first time, such as wrapping. Note; we kept the long plastic bags the longer pieces come in, in tact in order to store them back in each, to keep them from banging around in the bag. All the pieces of the set seem well designed and made. I would say one person could set it up easily. It also seems like, as long as you take care of it, it’ll last. There are black rubber ends to things TIP: keep them and put them back on to protect the pieces in storage.

In the end my wife and I are thrilled - not only to finally get to start using things - but with both the paddle/bag/ball/rules portion of the Champion Eclipse Graphite Complete Pickleball Set and the net part. together or separate, you’ll find a nice beginner and/or family set for a lot of fun. Our use will be varied, but we are happy to have this Champion Eclipse Graphite Complete Pickleball Set.
text_fidelity_b: Champion Eclipse Graphite Complete Pickleball Set | Includes 3.0 Portable Net System + 4 Graphite Pickleball Paddles + 4 Outdoor Pickleballs + Pickleball Duffel Bag + USAPA Rulebook

text_fidelity_a:
Seaview 180 Degree Panoramic Snorkel Mask- Full Face Design,Panoramic Teal,Large/Extra Large [[VIDEOID:3a1d0e8884973fd7767817b61417e9f7]] I've been snorkeling a few places around the world and I've learned just enough to know that good gear and good locations make all the difference.

I've had the chance to try out the Seaview 180 snorkeling mask from Wildhorn Outfitters. The Seaview 180 is different type of snorkel mask. The mask fits around your entire face - covering your eyes, nose and mouth.

I've experienced snorkeling in the Gulf of Mexico, off a deserted island in south america, in Belize, Thailand, and Nicaragua and Costa Rica. I felt like I wanted my own gear that fits and works right every time - so I finally ordered Wildhorn Outfitters Seaview 180 after having kept an eye on it for a while.

Over the last few months I've tried out a few products from Wildhorn outfitters and I've walked away impressed every time. This time was no different.

After trying this mask I had one big regret - not ordering this mask a few months ago. I really wish I could have used it last month in Central America but I know I will definitely be bringing it on my trip to Belize next year. Here's why:

Pros:

Visibility - It's hard to describe how amazing the visibility is in this mask. It is a completely different experience than any other snorkel equipment that I have ever used.

Breathing - With this mask the breathing experience is totally different. I'm not worried about breathing at all - which is kind of weird. When snorkeling I usually have to think about how I breathe - through my mouth and not my nose - keeping a tight seal around the mouthpiece - making sure not to breathe in too late after going under the water... you get the idea. With this mask I felt so much more comfortable and normal. Because the mask covers your entire face you can breathe out of mouth or nose. Also, if you try to breathe in when submerged no water actually enters your mask. You feel the pull of trying to breathe in without air but that's it. Also, if you get water in your mask the water will drain out the bottom of the mask when you lift your head out of the water.

Fog - When I tried the mask on at my house it fogged up a little but when I actually got in the water I had no issues with fog. I was planning on purchasing some anti-fog spray but now I think I'll delay that purchase and see if I actually need it in the future.

Go Pro Mount - I've used wrist mounts and other types of chest, head, and handheld mounts with a GoPro before and none of them really capture the footage how I want when snorkeling. I often spend too much time adjusting the head mount to make sure it's filming what I want it to film. With this setup I can set it up just how I want it and not worry about it being in the way or not being aimed the right way. Adjustment is also quick and easy.

Ease of use - This is the easiest snorkel mask I've ever used. It is a little shocking how quickly I got used to it. My young daughters would absolutely love masks of their own.

Cons:

Facial hair - You do need to be aware of how much facial hair you have when using this mask. Sometimes when I travel abroad I don't bother to bring a razor but with this mask I would probably bring one. Since the mask covers your entire nose and mouth it works better when I have recently shaved.

Overall:
If you snorkel regularly or are thinking of picking up equipment for your first snorkel adventure I can't recommend this mask more highly. I can't wait to use my mask again.
text_fidelity_b: Seaview 180 Degree Panoramic Snorkel Mask- Full Face Design,Panoramic Teal,Large/Extra Large

I quickly found out that this is not the case at all. This ring fits all 6 inch figures, but you will need to at least buy one WWE Super Striker figure to be able to use the one launching turn buckle.

The ring is easy to put together and doesn't take long- we spent about 20 minutes. You are going to want to spend another $10.00 for one of the Super Striker figures, as launching a figure from the turn buckle platform is just way too much fun! I purchased John Cena, and the kids love him. His feet are different to fit on the launcher.

The scaffold can move or even collapse if hit that holds the chain that holds the champion belt. Also if the launched Super Striker figure flies into the Titantron screen- the screen can get smashed- and of course be put back together for more hits. You can also use the platform on the turn buckle to hurl an opponent into the ring. The platform attaches to any of the ring posts for more fun in trying to reach the belt hanging from the scaffold.

Any 6 inch figure can play in the ring and stand on the ropes. We already own the Mattel WWE Wrestling Champion collection of 4 six inch figures and they all play in the ring- they just don't have the feet with holes to fly off the launching turn buckle. I've seen every 6 inch figure we have in the house wrestle in this ring- wrestlers, older GI Joes, a 6 inch Harry Potter, even some 6 inch animals- especially a bear. This ring is a lot of fun for the kids- and you really only need to spend another ten bucks for a Super Striker figure that they'll love launching into the ring!

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge 3 Fitness Activity Tracker I'm a Fitbit lover. I track everything with it; steps, heart rate, activity, sleep, food, BMI, body fat. All these metrics warm my geeky little heart and help me achieve my health goals. I own a Flex, an Alta HR, and the Aria 2 scale and have adored all of them. Because I love them so much, I gave my husband a Charge 3 for his birthday. I'm sorry to say, this Fitbit product is a total dud. The tracker will not sync with Fitbit's app. It worked for about 1 month then just stopped syncing with the app. We've tried every flavor of delete-reinstall-reset possible, all to no avail. There are hundreds, maybe thousands, of people who have this same issue, who have reported it to Fitbit, and the response is unfortunately not in keeping with the company's usual excellent customer service. All they will offer people is another Charge 3. You can't even swap the tracker for a less expense, older model that works with their app. Without the app, without the ability to track and review a history, the Charge 3 is little better than the freebie plastic pedometers your employer's health insurance plan hands out at their annual Open Enrollment fair. What's more than a little irksome is that Fitbit seems unwilling to admit there's a major software problem here. Seems obvious when one reads the Help forums. Why not 'fess up and tell us an estimate of when we can expect a software update? I don't get it. People will likely be patient and wait for the update if they know one is in the works. What is to be gained by pretending nothing is wrong? A lot of very unhappy customers, that's what.

Long story short: Don't buy this tracker. Get a different one. Maybe even one not made by Fitbit (sorry, Fitbit!)
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge 3 Fitness Activity Tracker

Fitbit One Wireless Activity Plus Sleep Tracker, Burgundy Just the facts: One burgundy Fitbit One activity tracker with clip on case, charger and sleep band.

Pros: This tracker is great for privacy, I can clip it on my bra and no one ever knows it's there. When I opened the box to set it up the battery was completely drained but I hooked it up to the charger and in less than 15 minutes was ready to go. Syncing with my pc and phone was extremely easy, just plug in and go. The app on my iPhone is what I normally use to view my data and it is extremely user friendly, I love doing challenges with my friends that have Fitbits as well. The tracker keeps up with steps, flights of stairs, distance, sleep and has silent alarms. What REALLY sells me on this particular tracker is it's accuracy though. I had a Charge HR before and ended up giving it to a friend because it frustrated me how often it was giving me credit for steps when I was just petting my dog watching tv. With the One not being strapped to my wrist it truly only counts my actual steps as steps. I've tested it by keeping the app open on my phone while doing different things that can trigger false steps and it is exceptionally accurate. I actually wear an Apple Watch and it consistently has 200-400 more steps at the end of a day than my One just due to the wrist movements.

Cons: With it not being on my wrist it's rather awkward to check it to see my steps during the day - to solve this I just check them on my phone app.

Would I recommend this? I would recommend this and often do!

Feel free to ask any questions and I'll be happy to answer them!
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit One Wireless Activity Plus Sleep Tracker, Burgundy
